module purpose: neorv32_wdt holds enable, lock, strict and timeout settings written from a bus request record, counts prescaler ticks taken from clkgen_i once enabled, restarts the count on a write that matches the constant reset_pwd_c, and drives a reset request on rstn_o when the count equals the timeout or when a write is refused in strict mode; it records the cause of the last reset and returns the settings and the cause on bus reads.

use-case flows.value: enable, strict and timeout settings taken from bus_req_i.data on a write to the control word while the lock is clear
lock bit, settable only while enable is 1, that refuses further control writes and turns each refused write into an access violation
count start: cnt_started rises on the first prescaler tick after enable; the enable is exported to the clock generator
tick counting: cnt increments on each registered tick, is cleared while disabled or on a restart, and is compared with the timeout
password-qualified restart: a write to the second word compares the data with reset_pwd_c; a match restarts the count, a mismatch flags an access violation
hardware reset request on timeout, or on an access violation in strict mode, driven out on rstn_o
reset cause recorded as debug, timeout or access violation
enable, lock, reset cause, strict and timeout returned on a read
rstn_sys_i clears the control fields, restart and violation flags, counter state and reset requests; rstn_ext_i alone clears the reset cause

conceptual assets.concept: Watchdog enable setting -- whether the watchdog counts and may request a reset
conceptual assets.reasoning: Configure flow: `ctrl.enable <= bus_req_i.data(ctrl_enable_c);` (line 94) under stb, rw, addr(2)='0' and ctrl.lock='0' (lines 90-93). The stored bit decides counting and both reset requests: it clears the counter when 0 (line 131, GATES cnt at occurrence 7), gates cnt_started (line 130), hw_rst_timeout (line 155) and hw_rst_access (line 156), and is a precondition for setting the lock (line 95). Integrity is Established: a wrong value changes whether a timeout or violation produces rstn_o. Availability is also Established: with enable at 0 no reset request is produced (lines 155-156). The value leaves the entity through `clkgen_en_o <= ctrl.enable;` (line 140, COPIES ctrl.enable at occurrence 2), an exported enable, which the clock rule does not exclude. ctrl.enable stores it (CLOCKED_BY clk_i at occurrence 3, line 94). The readback on bus_rsp_o.data (line 109) is not an exit: bus_rsp_o is a transport record (ack, err, data), and bus_req_i (addr, data, ben, stb, rw) is excluded as a setting point for the same reason.

conceptual assets.concept: Configuration lock -- freezes the watchdog settings until a system reset
conceptual assets.reasoning: Lock flow: `ctrl.lock <= bus_req_i.data(ctrl_lock_c) and ctrl.enable;` (line 95) can only be set while enabled; once set, `if (ctrl.lock = '0')` (line 93) refuses writes to enable, lock, strict and timeout (GATES at occurrence 3 on all four fields) and the else arm sets reset_force (line 99, GATES reset_force). Only rstn_sys_i clears it (line 76). Integrity is Established: a cleared lock lets the settings be rewritten, a wrongly set lock turns legitimate writes into violations. ctrl.lock stores the value (CLOCKED_BY clk_i at occurrence 4, line 95) and uses it in this entity through its GATES records. Its readback (line 110) goes only to the transport record bus_rsp_o, which is not reported.

conceptual assets.concept: Strict-mode setting -- whether an access violation causes a hardware reset
conceptual assets.reasoning: Configure flow: `ctrl.strict <= bus_req_i.data(ctrl_strict_c);` (line 96) under the same write and lock conditions. It decides `hw_rst_access <= ctrl.enable and ctrl.strict and reset_force;` (line 156, GATES hw_rst_access at occurrence 5). Integrity is Established: clearing it suppresses the violation reset, setting it adds one. ctrl.strict stores it (CLOCKED_BY clk_i at occurrence 3, line 96); its readback (line 112) goes only to the transport record.

conceptual assets.concept: Timeout threshold -- the count value at which the watchdog expires
conceptual assets.reasoning: Configure flow: `ctrl.timeout <= bus_req_i.data(ctrl_timeout_msb_c downto ctrl_timeout_lsb_c);` (line 97). The expiry decision compares the count with it: `cnt_timeout <= '1' when (cnt_started = '1') and (cnt = ctrl.timeout) else '0';` (line 144, CONSTRAINS cnt_timeout at occurrence 5). Integrity is Established: a different threshold moves or prevents the timeout reset (line 155). ctrl.timeout stores it (CLOCKED_BY clk_i at occurrence 3, line 97); its readback (line 113) goes only to the transport record.

conceptual assets.concept: Watchdog count state -- elapsed ticks since enable or the last restart, and whether counting has started
conceptual assets.reasoning: Operate flow: `cnt <= std_ulogic_vector(unsigned(cnt) + 1);` (line 134) on cnt_inc, cleared by `if (ctrl.enable = '0') or (reset_wdt = '1')` (lines 131-132); `cnt_started <= ctrl.enable and (cnt_started or prsc_tick);` (line 130) both are self-updating state. cnt is compared with the threshold (CONSTRAINS cnt_timeout at occurrence 6, line 144) and cnt_started qualifies counting and expiry (GATES cnt_inc at occurrence 3, line 129; GATES cnt_timeout at occurrence 6, line 144). Integrity is Established: a wrong count or start state moves or prevents the expiry decision. cnt stores (CLOCKED_BY clk_i at occurrence 4, line 134) and cnt_started stores (CLOCKED_BY clk_i at occurrence 4, line 130). Not listed: cnt_inc holds prsc_tick and cnt_started one clock later (GATED_BY both, line 129) and only gates cnt (line 133); prsc_tick is a bit of clkgen_i (line 141) that only enables counting steps, so clkgen_i is treated as a clock-enable input.

conceptual assets.concept: Password-qualified restart decision -- whether a write restarts the watchdog count
conceptual assets.reasoning: Restart flow: `if (bus_req_i.data(31 downto 0) = reset_pwd_c) then reset_wdt <= '1';` (lines 102-103) on a write with addr(2)='1' (lines 90-92); it is cleared every cycle (line 87). The decision clears the count (line 131, GATES cnt at occurrence 5). Integrity is Established: a restart without the matching word would keep the watchdog from expiring, and a missed restart would cause a timeout reset. reset_wdt stores the decision (CLOCKED_BY clk_i at occurrence 4, line 103). reset_pwd_c is a constant, not a candidate; no read path returns it (lines 109-113), but its confidentiality depends on context outside this file and is not claimed.

conceptual assets.concept: Access-violation reset -- a refused write (lock set or wrong password) and the hardware reset it requests in strict mode
conceptual assets.reasoning: reset_force is set by a write while locked (line 99) or a restart write whose data differs from reset_pwd_c (line 105), and cleared every other cycle (line 88). `hw_rst_access <= ctrl.enable and ctrl.strict and reset_force;` (line 156) turns it into a reset request, and `rstn_o <= not (hw_rst_timeout or hw_rst_access);` (line 161) drives it out; hw_rst_access also selects reset cause "11" (line 176). Integrity is Established: a missed violation flag or request suppresses the reset the strict mode requires, a false one resets the system. Availability is also Established: the request is produced on the cycle after the violation when enable and strict are 1. reset_force stores the violation flag (CLOCKED_BY clk_i at occurrence 4, line 99; GATES hw_rst_access); hw_rst_access stores the request (CLOCKED_BY clk_i at occurrence 3, line 156; SOURCES rstn_o, GATES reset_cause); rstn_o is the exit port (DERIVES_FROM hw_rst_access at occurrence 2, line 161).

conceptual assets.concept: Timeout expiry and reset request -- the decision that the count reached the threshold and the hardware reset it requests
conceptual assets.reasoning: cnt_timeout computes the expiry (line 144, CONSTRAINED_BY cnt and ctrl.timeout at occurrence 2, GATED_BY cnt_started). `hw_rst_timeout <= ctrl.enable and cnt_timeout and prsc_tick;` (line 155) registers the request, which drives `rstn_o <= not (hw_rst_timeout or hw_rst_access);` (line 161) and selects reset cause "10" (line 174). Integrity is Established: a false expiry resets the system, a suppressed one defeats the watchdog. Availability is also Established: when enabled and the count equals the threshold on a tick, the request is produced on the next clock edge (lines 154-155). cnt_timeout computes (occurrence 2, CONSTRAINED_BY cnt); hw_rst_timeout stores (CLOCKED_BY clk_i at occurrence 3, line 155; SOURCES rstn_o, GATES reset_cause); rstn_o is the exit port (DERIVES_FROM hw_rst_timeout at occurrence 2, line 161).

conceptual assets.concept: Reset cause record -- which event (debug, timeout, access violation) caused the last reset
conceptual assets.reasoning: Report flow: reset_cause takes "01" when rstn_dbg_i = '0' (lines 171-172), "10" on hw_rst_timeout (lines 173-174) and "11" on hw_rst_access (lines 175-176), inside the clocked arm (line 170); only rstn_ext_i clears it (lines 168-169), not rstn_sys_i, so the value is held across a system reset. It is returned on reads (line 111, CARRIES bus_rsp_o.data at occurrence 2, an output field). Integrity is Established: the reported cause must match the event that set it. reset_cause stores it (CLOCKED_BY clk_i at occurrence 4, line 172). rstn_dbg_i sets it: it is read in this entity to decide the value (GATES reset_cause at occurrence 2, line 171); it drives no SEQUENCES or RESETS record and is not in a reset arm, so the reset rule does not exclude it. hw_rst_timeout and hw_rst_access also decide it but are listed under their own concepts. rstn_ext_i is excluded as a reset input (RESETS reset_cause, line 168).
